title: Evil, Suffering, and Theodicy
research_question: How should the Way understand suffering, moral evil, natural evil, and the apparent tension between suffering and claims about divine goodness or power?
provisional_baseline: The Way may teach compassion, lament, resistance to preventable harm, care for sufferers, and epistemic restraint. It must not teach that all suffering is deserved or divinely scripted.

title: Salvation, Liberation, Healing, and Awakening
research_question: What, if anything, is the basic human problem and what constitutes its healing, liberation, reconciliation, awakening, or completion?
provisional_baseline: The Way may speak provisionally of healing, liberation, reconciliation, awakening, and wholeness, while refusing to collapse them into one metaphysical claim before evidence warrants it.

title: Death, Resurrection, Rebirth, and Afterlife
research_question: What happens at death, if anything, and what kinds of postmortem continuity are coherent or evidenced?
provisional_baseline: The Way adopts hope without fabrication: death is certain; grief is real; ultimate destiny remains an open question. Memorial practice may express hope while naming uncertainty.

title: Sexuality, Marriage, Family, and Intimate Ethics
research_question: What ethical principles should govern sexuality, marriage, partnership, family, celibacy, parenting, and intimate power?
provisional_baseline: Before settling disputed sexual theology, the Way can already require consent, non-exploitation, honesty, care, safeguarding, and equality before institutional processes. No Companion is required to marry, reproduce, remain married, or disclose intimate information to retain spiritual standing.

title: Violence, Nonviolence, Defense, and Peace
research_question: Does the Way require pacifism, permit defensive force, or recognize justifiable violence under limited conditions?
provisional_baseline: The Way adopts a presumption toward nonviolence and peacemaking but does not yet declare absolute pacifism. Religious authority never grants an independent license to harm.

title: Rites, Sacraments, Symbols, and Sacred Mediation
research_question: What can rites do, and do any rites mediate divine grace or spiritual reality beyond their communal, ethical, and psychological functions?
provisional_baseline: Rites may be used now as truthful communal practices whose claimed efficacy is no stronger than the evidence and theology supporting them.

title: Ordination, Ministry, Charisma, and Religious Office
research_question: Should the Way recognize an ordained clergy, and if so what is conferred by ordination?
provisional_baseline: Commissioning remains the operative authorization. Ordination stays reserved until theology requires something commissioning cannot truthfully express.

title: Sacred Time, Weekly Rhythm, Calendar, Fasting, and Festivals
research_question: How should the Way organize recurring sacred time without fabricating ancient authority or prematurely freezing a calendar?
provisional_baseline: Adopt recurring sacred rhythm before adopting a total calendar: regular prayer, weekly communal gathering/rest rhythm, periodic service and self-examination, and annual remembrance may develop experimentally with transparent revision.

title: Interreligious Identity, Dialogue, Conversion, and Dual Belonging
research_question: How should the Way relate to other religions and to Companions who retain, revise, or relinquish prior religious identities?
provisional_baseline: The Way practices neither "all religions are the same" nor "all others are false." It adopts disciplined hospitality: learn accurately, preserve disagreement, protect conscience, cooperate in good work, and test claims without coercion.
